About Space City Home Network Space City Home Network is the Astros' own regional sports network, launched in October 2023 after owner Jim Crane acquired the broadcast rights from AT&T SportsNet Southwest. Unlike many RSNs across the country that have faced financial turmoil in recent years, SCHN operates with long-term carriage agreements and is widely regarded as one of the most stable regional sports networks in baseball. The 2026 broadcast team features Todd Kalas on play-by-play, Geoff Blum as color analyst, and Julia Morales as sideline reporter — a familiar crew that Astros fans have come to know well. SCHN airs the vast majority of Houston's games not claimed by national broadcast windows, making it the centerpiece of any Astros streaming setup. What About Out-of-Market Astros Fans? If you live outside the Houston market and can't access SCHN locally, Fubo still has you covered. MLB.TV is available as an add-on through Fubo, letting you stream every out-of-market regular season game live and on demand. This is the gold standard for fans of teams outside their home market, giving you access to all 162 games regardless of where you live. Note that standard MLB.TV blackout restrictions apply: if you're in the Astros' home market, those games will be blacked out on MLB.TV (which is why SCHN via Fubo is the right solution for local fans). The 2026 Astros: A Team Worth Watching Houston enters 2026 strong after their 2025 campaign. The Astros held a seven-game division lead in early July before a run of injuries proved proved difficult to come back from. The front office responded decisively this offseason. The headline addition is Japanese right-hander Tatsuya Imai, who posted a 1.92 ERA in Japan in 2025 and joins as a front-of-rotation arm. The return of Carlos Correa at third base adds postseason-caliber depth, and Hunter Brown enters 2026 as one of the most exciting young starters in the American League after his breakout 2023 ERA of 2.43. With a revamped rotation including Yordan Alvarez back after last season’s hand fracture, the Astros are firmly in the AL West conversation — making this a season well worth streaming from Opening Day to the final out. 2026 Houston Astros Season: Key Dates to Know Spring Training Begins: February 20, 2026 World Baseball Classic: March 4–17, 2026 (Houston's Daikin Park hosts pool play and quarterfinals) Opening Day: March 26, 2026 Jackie Robinson Day: April 15, 2026 All-Star Week: July 11–14, 2026 Home Run Derby: July 13, 2026 Trade Deadline: August 3, 2026 MLB at Field of Dreams: August 13, 2026 Postseason Begins: September 29, 2026 World Series: October 23, 2026 Notably, Houston's Daikin Park (formerly Minute Maid Park) hosts the 2026 World Baseball Classic pool play and quarterfinal rounds in early March — adding a major international event to the city's baseball calendar before the regular season even begins.
